P01.note: Introductory 'Although' clause ends after the object: 'copied the exemplar,' then main clause 'the illuminators ... departed'. A reads 'copied' intransitively and strands 'the exemplar' before the real subject; C puts a semicolon after a subordinate clause.
P01.not_hard_because: 'that model' in the main clause names the exemplar, so the object visibly belongs to the copying clause; same intro-clause-boundary template as P07.

P02.note: Elliptical auxiliary for 'loses': plural 'samples' + simple present lexical verb -> 'do'. 'have' tempts but would need an elided past participle.
P02.not_hard_because: 'samples' sits immediately before the blank and hands over the plural; ellipsis-aux template shared with P03, P04, P11.

P03.note: Ellipsis of 'dependable' after a be-verb in the main clause ('are not dependable') -> 'is'; singular 'bath'. 'does' attracts solvers who default to do-support.
P03.not_hard_because: 'bath' is the noun right before the blank and the main clause prints 'are not dependable', handing over be-ellipsis; same template as P02/P04/P11.

P04.note: 'much as a student ... often does' mirrors 'recalls' (present, lexical) with singular 'student'. 'do' attracts via plural 'formulas'/'mornings' adjacent to the blank.
P04.not_hard_because: the parallel verb 'recalls' and the present 'rehearses' fix both aux type and tense; third ellipsis item in the render (P02, P03, P11).

P05.note: Compound subject 'Marigolds ... and a cover crop' is plural; present 'is not planted' fixes tense -> 'are holding'. Singular 'mustard' next to blank is the trap.
P05.not_hard_because: 'and' joining two subjects is the textbook plural signal and the 'as long as ... is' clause hands over present tense.

P06.note: Plural 'sketches' -> 'depict'; the thing depicted is the singular 'window' -> 'it'. 'window' adjacent to the blank pulls toward 'depicts'.
P06.not_hard_because: the head noun is the first noun of the sentence as in every agreement item here, and 'that original window' is the only candidate referent; same 2x2 pronoun+verb grid as P13, P19, P35.

P07.note: 'While the organist played,' (intransitive) then 'the pipes mounted highest ... often sounded flat'. B and C let 'played the pipes' read as verb+object, leaving 'often sounded' without a subject; D puts a colon after a dependent clause.

P08.note: Complete clause 'recorded what the households had in common' introduces a three-item list -> colon. A's comma blurs the list into the clause; C semicolon before a non-clause list.
P08.not_hard_because: 'had in common' plus the three-part list after the blank announce a colon; same colon-before-specification template as P15.

P09.note: Plural 'readings', past 'in the decades preceding the port's first ... gauge' -> 'were taken'. 'pier' singular next to blank and present 'According to' tempt.
P09.not_hard_because: the time phrase 'in the decades preceding' settles tense and the subject's head noun is the first noun; this is one of ~14 number-x-tense grid items (see near_duplicates).

P10.note: Two independent clauses ('they spent ... in the cold, thin air' / 'the remedy ... did little'); period. The second clause is a verdict, not an explanation, so the colon (strongest distractor) does not fit; B is a comma splice.
P10.not_hard_because: once 'did little' is found as the second main verb the boundary is obvious; the only live competitor is the colon, and the second clause clearly does not elaborate the first.

P11.note: Ellipsis of 'dwindled' from 'has dwindled': plural 'vacancies' -> 'have too'. 'has too' attracts via 'board'; 'are too' has no be-antecedent.
P11.not_hard_because: the earlier 'has dwindled' hands over the perfect auxiliary and 'vacancies' the number; fourth ellipsis item (P02, P03, P04).

P12.note: Plural 'cashiers', completed past 'during the paper-ticket era that preceded swipe cards' -> 'were logging'. 'have been logging' tempts via present 'who staff'.
P12.not_hard_because: the time phrase 'during the paper-ticket era that preceded' gives the tense outright; grid template.

P13.note: Singular 'canister' -> 'is towed'; the towing agents are the 'drones' two sentences back -> 'them'. 'by it' attracts because the only nearby singular nouns ('battery', 'vent', 'crust') are wrong referents.

P14.note: Plural possessive: the following sentence says 'The contractors later disagreed about ... those copies', so the tally is the contractors'. 'contractor's' is attractive because 'tally' is singular and nothing before the blank signals plurality.

P15.note: 'a hidden cost more heavily than the ticket price' is complete and the cost is then specified -> colon. B semicolon introduces a fragment.
P15.not_hard_because: 'a hidden cost' announces a specification and two of the three distractors are unpunctuated mash-ups nobody would choose; same template as P08.

P16.note: Restrictive participle: the team examined the specimens gathered along the margin, contrasted in the next sentence with meteorites from the interior; commas would make the location incidental. A (comma) is attractive as a natural pause.

P17.not_hard_because: 'serves' and 'borrow' hand over present and the head noun is the first noun of the subject; grid template.

P18.note: 'has always ... subsided': the perfect auxiliary is split from its participle by 'within an hour of the afternoon melt peak'. 'is always' reads naturally until 'subsided' arrives eight words later; singular 'level'.

P19.note: Plural 'veterinarians' -> 'have measured'; the antibody levels belong to the chicks/birds -> 'their'. 'its' could be pulled toward 'grower' or 'spray'.
P19.not_hard_because: 'veterinarians' sits right before the blank, and both rules point the same way (plural/plural), so solving the verb nearly solves the pronoun; pronoun grid with P06, P13, P35.

P20.not_hard_because: 'chief' immediately before the blank names one person, and no distractor survives once a possessive is needed before 'graft'; possessive template with P14, P34.

P21.note: Plural 'Wafers', past ('scrapped', 'had leaked') -> 'were also [unfit]'; be-verb split from 'unfit' by 'by the inspectors' revised standards'. 'have also' would need a participle.
P21.not_hard_because: 'scrapped' and 'had leaked' settle past and 'Wafers' opens the sentence; split-auxiliary shape shared with P18, P26.

P22.note: Plural 'names'; 'since the volume entered the palace library' requires present perfect -> 'have been concealed'. 'sheet' tempts singular.
P22.not_hard_because: the word 'since' settles tense wherever it appears in these grid items (P22, P32's 'for nine growing seasons').

P23.note: Plural 'tracks', a single past event 'on the night of the club's closing concert' -> 'were performed'. The 'since' in the relative clause baits present perfect ('have been performed').

P24.note: 'first in X, then [in] Y' is one clause with a parallel phrase; comma before 'then'. Semicolon/colon would need an independent clause after them.
P24.not_hard_because: 'first' earlier in the sentence announces the 'then' series, and nothing after the blank is a clause, so semicolon and colon fail at a glance.

P25.note: Two independent clauses: 'a grower moved ... to the orchard' / 'a sheltered block ... flowered eleven days later'. A reads the block as an appositive to 'orchard' and strands 'flowered'; colon would need an explanation.

P26.note: 'seldom are ... handling': progressive be split from its participle by 'during the early years of an apprenticeship'. 'seldom do' attracts solvers primed by the rarely-do ellipsis items; 'master's studio' baits 'is'.

P27.note: Heavy-object shift: 'set aside [for emergency repairs] the surplus ...'; no punctuation may separate the verb from its object. The fronted phrase makes a comma feel natural.

P28.note: Mass noun 'milk' is singular; present 'shows' -> 'is kept'.
P28.not_hard_because: 'milk' is unmistakably singular and there is no plural noun between it and the blank to act as a trap; 'shows' hands over tense.

P29.note: Singular 'apprentice' (not 'compositors'), past 'when a candle tipped over' -> 'was inking'.
P29.not_hard_because: 'tipped' gives tense and the head noun is the first noun of the subject; grid template.

P30.note: Singular 'catalogue', past 'during the slide-rule era's closing years' -> 'was being indexed'. 'photographs' and 'two technicians' bait plural.
P30.not_hard_because: 'during the ... closing years' gives the tense and the subject's first noun is the head; grid template.

P31.note: Singular 'Turnout', single past event 'during the mayoral runoff that autumn' -> 'was typical'. 'renters'/'blocks' bait plural.
P31.not_hard_because: 'that autumn' fixes a past event and the head noun opens the sentence; grid template.

P32.note: Plural 'probes', duration 'for nine growing seasons' plus present 'their readings show' -> 'have been measuring'.
P32.not_hard_because: 'for nine growing seasons' is a duration phrase that hands over the perfect; same as 'since' in P22.

P33.note: Plural 'Floods' (not 'spillway'); a completed result relevant now ('which is why inspecting ... requires divers') -> 'have carved'.
P33.not_hard_because: the present 'requires' hands over present perfect, the same present-consequence cue as P32 and P39.

P34.note: 'catalog' is the verb: 'the archivists catalog entries ... on acid-free cards'. B needs 'catalogs'; C/D turn 'catalog entries' into a noun phrase and leave the sentence without a main verb.

P35.note: Singular 'director' -> 'was checking'; the thing checked is the family's 'questionnaire' -> 'it'. 'them' baits toward 'notes'.
P35.not_hard_because: 'director' sits at the end of the subject next to the blank and 'a family's questionnaire' is the obvious singular referent; pronoun grid with P06, P13, P19.

P36.convention: restrictive reduced relative: 'the observatory's largest dish warped by decades of wind' can be read as 'the largest of the warped dishes'
P36.note: With 'largest' identifying one dish, the participle is nonessential -> comma. B is attractive and arguably legal as a restrictive reading; D colon has no list/explanation.

P37.convention: a comma setting off a nonessential trailing modifier ('..., out of a small harbor') is standard
P37.note: Close appositive 'ship Kestrel' takes no comma (C fragment, A unpaired dash). Whether 'out of a small harbor' needs a comma is style, not rule, so D is also defensible.
P37.not_hard_because: the vessel-name construction is familiar and the period and lone dash are visibly wrong, leaving only B vs D.

P38.note: 'found [that] the dispensers ... were used' - a noun-clause object takes no punctuation after the verb. Dash/comma/semicolon all split verb from object.
P38.not_hard_because: after P27 the 'no mark between verb and object' key is a pattern in this render, and 'were used' later makes the object clause plain.

P39.convention: simple past for a completed action with present relevance is accepted in edited American English when no time frame is stated ('The optic was superseded by LEDs, and the beam ... is whiter')
P39.note: Singular 'optic'; present consequence ('the beam that pilots see ... is whiter') favours 'has been superseded'. No past time marker excludes simple past, so C is defensible.
P39.not_hard_because: the head noun opens the sentence and the present-tense consequence clause hands over the perfect, same cue as P32/P33.

P40.note: Singular 'reel'; present 'whenever a technician threads' -> 'is brittle'. 'feature'/'films' are the traps.
P40.not_hard_because: 'whenever ... threads' fixes the present and the head noun is the first noun of the subject; grid template.

tells: Head noun = first noun of the subject: in every number item the subject's head is the first noun at the start of the clause and a later prepositional/relative noun of the opposite number is the trap (P05 mustard, P06 window, P09 pier, P12 schools, P17 farmer/title, P29 compositors, P30 photographs, P31 renters/blocks, P32 vines, P33 spillway, P39 panes, P40 feature). A solver who always agrees with the first noun scores every one.

Tense is always handed over by a time phrase or present verb AFTER the blank: 'since' -> present perfect (P22), duration 'for nine growing seasons' -> perfect (P32), 'during the ... era/years' -> simple past (P12, P30), a present consequence clause ('requires divers', 'pilots see', 'readings show') -> present perfect (P32, P33, P39), 'whenever ... threads'/'serves'/'shows' -> present (P17, P28, P40). Only P23 baits the 'since' cue.
The number-x-tense 2x2 option grid (sg/pl x present/past or perfect) appears in 14+ items; the grid shape itself announces that exactly two features must be read.

Pronoun items use the same 2x2 grid (verb number x pronoun number) and the pronoun's referent is always the one non-subject noun of the right kind (window P06, drones P13, birds P19, questionnaire P35).

Ellipsis items (P02, P03, P04, P11): the key aux always copies the verb type of the other clause (lexical -> do/does, be -> is, perfect -> have), and the number comes from the noun immediately before the blank.
No-punctuation key whenever the blank sits between a verb and its object/complement (P27, P38) or a noun and a restrictive modifier (P16, P37).
Colon is the key whenever the preceding words announce a specification ('had in common' P08, 'a hidden cost' P15) and loses when the next clause is a separate event or verdict (P10, P25).
